title: Light-field display resolution-density tradeoff
bottleneck: Light-field displays reproduce correct focus cues by emitting many angular views, but dividing pixels among views slashes spatial resolution: a 4K panel becomes effectively sub-HD per view. Capturing or rendering dozens of views multiplies compute, and the microlens arrays add bulk. Resolution high enough for text becomes impractical.
why_it_blocks: Light fields could fix VAC without eye tracking, but the resolution cost makes them unusable for productivity. The tradeoff between correct focus and sharp text is fundamental to the approach.
current_state: Prototype light-field near-eye displays exist with limited resolution; compressive and neural approaches aim to recover detail. No product-grade light-field headset has shipped. Microlens arrays add thickness and optical loss, working against the compactness that near-eye displays require. Capturing real-world light fields needs dense camera arrays, so content creation is as hard as display.
